structure: A single short Markdown ruling file, 60 lines (workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-25.md), from Ian, dated 25 November 2026, on pagination of the address book's lists and the party pickers, raised by the manage-notifications pre-flight when registering ruling:paul-2026-11-05 surfaced a conflict with ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 over req-611. It is laid out as: a one-paragraph framing of what raised it; the owner's words as a two-line block quote ("Pagination should be kept. We want it. It was removed previously in error. We actually fixed that theme removing it with a bug EUDPA-827"), which is the ruling proper and the only verbatim source; a "What was asked" section setting the two opposed readings of req-611 side by side as two bullets (Paul's point 8 and Ian's 23 November point 6, the latter quoted); and a "Decided" section of five numbered points, the second carrying three indented code-citation bullets naming address book files (RequestedListFilters.java, AddressController.java, ListPaging.java) and a closing paragraph of reasoning. After point 5 comes an unnumbered closing paragraph marked as the orchestrator's call, applying the ruling and explicitly open to being overruled, on the plants contact picker's page size moving from five to eight, citing insfrontend:src/server/app/features/address-book/list/list.controller.js:49 and REQ-INS-ADDR-013. Scope is the whole file and nothing is left out. At 60 lines it is far inside one agent's reading, so it is one part.

parts.title: Whole ruling
parts.scope: The whole file: the framing paragraph, the owner's block-quoted words, the two bullets under "What was asked", the five numbered points under "Decided" with point 2's three code citations and closing reasoning, and the unnumbered orchestrator's-call paragraph at the foot. There is no other part.
covers: The framing: the ruling was raised by the manage-notifications pre-flight, where registering ruling:paul-2026-11-05 surfaced a conflict with ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 over req-611
The block-quoted ruling itself, verbatim: pagination should be kept, it is wanted, its earlier removal was an error, and EUDPA-827 fixed the theme that removed it

What was asked: the two opposed readings of req-611 — ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8 (the address book's list and every address picker keep pagination, the list API pages with page and pageSize of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, and no unpaginated requirement is built) against ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 (req-611 unaffected, the role-scoped list staying unpaginated because the endpoint takes no role, filters by role itself, then pages what is left for display)

Decided point 1: pagination is kept and its removal was an error; every address book list and every address picker pages; no requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated
Decided point 2: req-611's 'unpaginated' clause is dropped and ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 is superseded on that point alone, its premise no longer being true of the service

Decided point 2's three code citations, each as its own claim of what the service does today: RequestedListFilters.java (a list request's filters are searchTerm, countryCodes, roles and searchRoles), AddressController.java (lists the caller's live addresses, newest first, one page at a time, page 1-based defaulting to 1, pageSize from ListPaging.MIN_PAGE_SIZE to MAX_PAGE_SIZE defaulting to DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE, taking roles and searchRoles alongside), and ListPaging.java (1 to 100, default 25, exactly the bounds ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8 names)

Decided point 2's closing reasoning: the role filter runs in the service before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong; "the list endpoint takes no role" described an earlier address book, not the one on main; Paul's point 8 stands in full and is the position to distil

Decided point 3: the rest of ruling:ian-2026-11-23 stands — the party pickers page at eight, the one-page clause of inc-087's acceptance criteria 7, 8 and 9 stays dropped, req-594 and req-595 stay dropped, the "Selected address" restatement comes back with the paging, and the two rulings differed only on whether the address book's own list API was one of the paged lists

Decided point 4: EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed — trade-imports-animals-frontend 0d1d606d, "fix(EUDPA-827): page the live animals party pickers at eight, naming the chosen address (#510)", merged to main on 24 November, with this workspace's 1ec8d9b7 for the behaviour spec; the live animals pickers need no further work

Decided point 5: conflict c-292 is settled — the plants contact picker keeps its pagination and its 'Selected address' inset, nothing drops either, and it takes the shared layout change (req-1964) as its default already said

The orchestrator's call at the foot, recorded as the orchestrator's rather than the owner's and flagged as open to being overruled: the plants contact picker's page size moves from five to eight so every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses (insfrontend:src/server/app/features/address-book/list/list.controller.js:49, REQ-INS-ADDR-013), on the ground that the ruling settles that a picker pages but not how many a page holds
The open point the closing paragraph leaves: whether the plants contact picker should stay at five — a gap claim, not a decision, since the ruling asks to be told
Any other gap the ruling leaves open on what it touches, recorded as a gap claim
